subject: Proposal: amortization / voucher exchange for renewal uplift
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Eliza Gomez <eliza.gomez@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: amortization / voucher exchange for renewal uplift

Hi Eliza —

Thanks again for taking the time yesterday. Per our conversation about Brightline's anticipated mid-contract growth, attached is a short usage extract (Q3) and an initial amortization/voucher-exchange proposal that would help smooth the uplift impact to Brightline's cashflow while preserving unit economics for Redwood. High-level: 

- Option A (Amortized top-up): Brightline pays an upfront prorated uplift and we amortize the net credit over the remaining term (monthly credit against invoices).
- Option B (Voucher exchange): Brightline takes a voucher for the uplift amount that can be drawn against future usage; voucher expires at renewal and can be exchanged for credits at co-term if unused.

Both options include a small implementation credit we discussed (5% of uplift) to offset engineering onboarding. I've attached a proposed schedule (Proposed_Amortization_Schedule_v2.xlsx) and a 1-page comparison.

Ask: can you confirm which path procurement prefers so we can draft an amendment and procurement-ready language for DocuSign? If procurement wants the voucher route we should also confirm the preferred expiry and any PO constraints.

If it helps, Kimberly and Ben are looped here — they can provide the invoice phasing and discount math.

Thanks,
Logan
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
attachments: [Brightline_Usage_Report_Q3.csv, Proposed_Amortization_Schedule_v2.xlsx]
From: Eliza Gomez <eliza.gomez@brightlinehealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@brightlinehealth.com
Date: 2026-10-06T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: amortization / voucher exchange for renewal uplift

Logan —

Appreciate the clear options. Procurement wants the voucher approach in principle (keeps finance happy), but they have two constraints: 1) voucher must be usable across teams (not tied to a single project SKU), and 2) voucher expiry needs a 12-month window after renewal rather than immediate co-term expiration.

Also, can you confirm if unused voucher value remains refundable or if we receive credits only? We need that detail for our CFO.

I've CC'd procurement who will share any PO formatting requirements.

Best,
Eliza
Head of Product Partnerships — Brightline Health
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Eliza Gomez <eliza.gomez@brightlinehealth.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-08T08:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: amortization / voucher exchange for renewal uplift

Eliza / team —

Thanks for the quick steer. A few clarifications on the voucher model and a practical ops path we typically use: 

- Voucher scope: we can issue a tenant-level voucher (usable across teams and projects) — we'll list it as an account credit in our billing system and it can be applied to any ingestion/generation usage.
- Expiry: 12 months post-renewal is fine. We typically set a hard expiry date and communicate it upfront; unused voucher balance is non-refundable but can be converted to invoice credit at renewal if agreed in advance (that gives Brightline options while preserving accounting predictability for Redwood).
- Governance: when a voucher is created we add a short amendment with the voucher ID, expiry, and redemption instructions; no change to base license pricing.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Logan and I will prepare a 1-page amendment with voucher ID, expiry (12 months post-renewal), redemption scope, and non-refundable language but with a renewal-conversion clause.
2) I'll include a sample PO appendix (procurement-friendly layout) to make it easier for your finance team.

If that sounds right, Logan — can you confirm the uplift dollar amount you want us to put in the draft and whether the 5% implementation credit stays?

Cheers,
Ben
Senior Sales Manager — Redwood Inference

Eliza / procurement / Ben / Kim —

Thanks — that's helpful. Based on Q3 run-rate and the expansion scope Brightline signaled, the uplift number we discussed is $180,000. I recommend we show $180k in the draft voucher amendment and keep the 5% implementation credit (so net voucher value = $171,000 drawn as account credit).

Kimberly — can you spin up the amendment draft and the PO appendix with those numbers? Ben, if you can include the redemption clause and renewal-conversion language that would be great. I can route the DocuSign link to Eliza and procurement once it's ready.

Logistics note: procurement asked for one small addition — a short acceptance checklist (3 bullets) that confirms voucher ID, expiry, and that the voucher is account-level. If we add those 3 bullets to the amendment cover page procurement should be able to sign without additional redlines.

I'll target EOD Thursday to have the DocuSign link ready.

Best,
Logan
